entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Konstantinos Phokas, a prominent Byzantine aristocrat and general, played a crucial role in the military resurgence of the Byzantine Empire during the mid-10th century, particularly against the Hamdanid Emirate. As the son of Bardas Phokas the Elder, a distinguished general, and brother to the future emperor Nikephoros II Phokas, Konstantinos was a central figure in the Phokas family's ascent to military and political dominance. His career was embedded within the broader context of the Byzantine-Arab Wars, where the empire sought to reclaim lost territories in Anatolia and the Levant, marking a period of aggressive expansion under the Macedonian dynasty.

Konstantinos Phokas distinguished himself in several key campaigns in eastern Anatolia, serving under Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos and later Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos. He participated in the strategic operations that led to significant Byzantine victories, including engagements against the formidable Hamdanid emir Sayf al-Dawla. His military acumen was particularly evident in the systematic consolidation of Byzantine control over border regions, weakening the Arab emirates' hold on Cappadocia and Cilicia through a combination of pitched battles and sieges. While specific details of his individual commands are sometimes overshadowed by the collective achievements of the Phokas family, his contributions were vital to the sustained pressure on the eastern frontier.
